novelty.reasoning: Core claim: a cheap linear probe on pre-step activations can predict whether the upcoming reasoning step will be causally load-bearing, and this signal can drive an attention-free detail-budget allocator. Closest prior family is Thought Anchors / TTS / MI-Peaks for importance labeling, plus ROI/meta-cognitive and budget-guidance work for budgeting. The genuine delta is the prospective, pre-emission prediction at step boundary and the deployability angle of avoiding attention matrices. This is meaningfully different from retrospective importance estimation, but the conceptual leap is moderate because it sits very close to prospective routing / meta-cognition and could reduce to difficulty/position proxies.
revision_notes: State a sharper falsifiable novelty claim: pre-step causal importance prediction, not just importance or compression.
Explicitly distinguish from ROI/meta-cognitive pre-generation cost prediction and from any prospective step-routing work in the related-work section.
Add evidence that the signal is not just difficulty, length, or position.
Include a direct comparison to a simple pre-step heuristic baseline and to representation-change predictors.

impact.reasoning: Problem: compress reasoning traces while preserving accuracy. Who cares: efficient-reasoning, interpretability, and inference-systems folks. If the method works, it changes when and how budget is allocated during CoT generation, potentially enabling cheaper deployment without attention-matrix materialization. That is practically relevant. However, downstream change is bounded: it is an optimization for inference-time efficiency on reasoning models, not a broad capability advance, and the benefit likely depends on model family/task. The so what is real but not transformative unless it consistently beats attention-based and budget-guidance baselines at meaningful token savings.
revision_notes: Quantify expected system-level gains beyond token savings: latency, memory, throughput, or cost.
Show a deployment scenario where attention-free pre-emission routing materially changes inference economics.
Add one broader impact angle beyond token accuracy tradeoffs, e.g. scalable reasoning on long-horizon tasks.
Clarify whether gains transfer across models/tasks or are narrow to the chosen benchmarks.

review.reasoning: The proposal is coherent and testable, with a clear pipeline: generate importance labels, train a linear probe, validate causally, then deploy as a budget allocator. Strengths are concreteness and experimental breadth. Main gaps: related work is somewhat overstated (no prior work asks is likely too strong given nearby prospective/meta-cognitive work); the key claim may collapse into a difficulty/position proxy; causal validation needs strong controls; and the allocator could underperform attention-based or uniform budget baselines despite good AUROC. Feasibility is plausible but label generation is compute-heavy and noisy. Missing ablations include: first-token vs full-pre-step features, linear vs nonlinear probe, per-layer probe choice, label noise sensitivity, cross-model transfer, calibration/threshold sweeps, and whether gains persist after controlling for step length and problem difficulty.
revision_notes: Tone down the absolute novelty claim and add a tighter, specific positioning against prospective budget-prediction and meta-cognitive routing work.
Add controls for difficulty, step position, token length, and answer entropy to rule out proxy explanations.
Include ablations on layer selection, probe complexity, and using only the first few step tokens vs the boundary state.
Report calibration and threshold robustness, not just AUROC.
Add direct head-to-heads with uniform compression, simple heuristics, and strongest budget-guidance baselines.
Specify causal steering protocol precisely and pre-register what counts as successful causal evidence.
Include cross-model and cross-dataset transfer to show the signal is not family-specific.
